title: Parenchyma cells are generally rhombic dodecahedra, ideal froths tetrakaidecahedra

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Parenchyma cells are generally rhombic dodecahedra, ideal froths tetrakaidecahedra

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A perfectly fluid froth of equal cells is divided into Kelvin’s fourteen-sided tetrakaidecahedra, but in plant parenchyma, given restraint and imperfect fluidity, the cells generally take the rhombic dodecahedral form even under symmetrical conditions.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Accordingly, it is very probably the case that, in the parenchymatous tissue, under the actual conditions of restraint and of very imperfect fluidity, it is after all the rhombic dodecahedral configuration which, even under perfectly symmetrical conditions, is generally assumed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Rhombic dodecahedra versus tetrakaidecahedra”. Scope: isolated cells of symmetrical plant parenchyma of near-equal cell size

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two geometric alternatives are sharply distinguishable in segmented volumes. Existing public microscopy can test selected tissues, but full 3D face resolution and the claim's 'generally' scope are limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Segment equal-sized plant parenchyma cells in 3D, classify face topology and geometry, and compare frequencies of rhombic dodecahedra and fourteen-faced Kelvin-like cells.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Few datasets resolve complete cell faces over large parenchyma volumes.

Cells are rarely equal-sized or perfectly symmetric.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Face number is a clean discriminator between the rhombic dodecahedron and Kelvin's fourteen-sided cell, and public segmentations make the count feasible. Those segmentations are meristems and early embryos rather than mature equal-celled parenchyma such as pith. The ideal can be tested in a restricted tissue class and not yet across the stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count faces and face shapes of interior cells in symmetrical, near-equal parenchyma. A mode near twelve rhombic faces would support the dodecahedral claim; a mode near fourteen with hexagonal and square faces would support Kelvin's tetrakaidecahedron instead.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Meristem and embryo cells are a young, growing subset of the symmetrical parenchyma the claim is about.

Surface cells must be excluded, because the twelve-versus-fourteen contrast is about interior cells of a bulk foam.
